newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares extend losses amid political tension.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares extend losses amid political tension.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply on Wednesday in continued downward spiral sparked by political tension haunting the markets this week, bringing three-day losses to 14.9 percent.

The IMKB National-100 closed 71 points, or 4.92 percent lower at 1,372, after rebounding slightly from a day's low of 1,361. Trade volume shrank to 15.20 trillion lira ($122.5 million) from Tuesday's 28.73 trillion ($232.2 million).

Brokers said the market would wait for the outcome of Thursday's cabinet meeting, the first after secularist generals warned the Islamist-led coalition at last Friday's National Security Council (MGK) meeting to rein in what they saw as rising Islamist zeal.
They expect reaction buys after the recent steep falls, but not a major recovery unless political stability is restored.

"Political tension continues since the MGK meeting which causes investors to prefer to sell. But today's most important aspect was lower volume which may be a sign that the sharp falls may cease," said Tuncay Tursucu from General Finans securities.
